Subject: Post-call recap + MAP draft (Integration build plan)

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Per our discovery session, attached is a first-draft Mutual Action Plan focusing on the Integration Build Plan milestone: SDK integration, streaming, tool calling, and structured outputs. High-level recap below and asks to keep momentum: 

Summary / goals:
- Objective: Ship production integration supporting SDK-based calls (Python/Node), streaming token-level responses, and tool-calling hooks for 3rd-party systems.
- Success metrics: 100ms median token latency on common flows, end-to-end demo with tool-calls in QA, and structured JSON outputs for ingestion.
- Target close date: 2026-04-30 (target contract execution / first production rollout).

Proposed MAP milestones (see attached ACME_MAP_Draft_v1.xlsx):
1) Integration design sign-off (owner: Acme eng + Redwood PM) — target 2026-03-26
2) SDK integration (owners: Redwood SDK team / Acme eng) — target 2026-04-09
3) Streaming & KV caching bench (owners: Redwood infra eng) — target 2026-04-16
4) Tool-calling integration (owners: Acme eng / Redwood SRE) — target 2026-04-23
5) Structured output schema & validation (owners: Acme data + Redwood API) — target 2026-04-20
6) Production rollout (owners: Acme + Redwood ops) — target 2026-04-30

Dependencies we flagged today:
- Formal schema for structured outputs from Acme (example payloads)
- VPN / VPC peering windows for Private deployment or access to test endpoints
- Signing of standard SOW / security addendum for SOC2 evidence

Asks / next steps:
- Please confirm owners for the Acme side in reply (especially SDK and tool-calling owners).
- Can we lock a 60-min technical sync with your eng team next week? I proposed Mon/Tue.

Attachments: ACME_MAP_Draft_v1.xlsx, integration-checklist.pdf

Thanks — looking forward to progressing.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0138

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the recap and the MAP draft. A few clarifying questions from our eng team after a quick skim:

1) SDK languages — we primarily build in Node and Python; will Redwood support both SDKs out of the box or do we need to wrap a generic client?
2) Streaming semantics — can you confirm whether streaming will provide partial JSON tokens and how you recommend rehydrating structured outputs on our side?
3) Tool calling — we need to understand the auth model you expect for tool callbacks (signed webhook vs mutual TLS).
4) Schema validation — we can provide example payloads by EOD Tue; is there an expected schema versioning approach?

Owners on our side (provisional):
- SDK/Integration: Samir Rao (samir.rao@acmecloud.com)

We can do a 60-min tech deep-dive on Tue 24 Mar at 10am PT. That work for you and your eng?

Cheers,
Alex

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + MAP draft (Integration build plan)

Alex — great, thanks for the quick replies and provisional owners. Tue 24 Mar 10am PT works for the tech sync; I sent a calendar invite to all.

Quick answers up-front and an updated MAP attached (ACME_MAP_Draft_v2.xlsx) with explicit Redwood owners:
- SDK languages: Redwood maintains official SDKs for Python and Node. Samir can use either; we will assign a dedicated SDK liaison for code samples and CI integration.
- Streaming semantics: partial tokens are streamed; for structured outputs we recommend emitting a final JSON payload as a single final chunk (we provide a "structured_output" flag on responses). We'll include example rehydration code in the SDK samples.
- Tool calling auth: default is signed webhook tokens; for higher-security deployments we support mutual TLS or KMS-signed HMAC. We'll surface options in the integration checklist.
- Schema versioning: Redwood supports a simple semantic version on the schema object (x.y.z). We can add a compatibility check in our client samples.

Updated owners (Redwood side):
- Integration design sign-off: Laura Bennett (CS PM) 
- SDK integration (Python/Node): Dev Patel (SDK lead)
- Streaming & KV caching bench: Rishi Malhotra (infra eng)
- Tool-calling integration (webhooks / mTLS): Dev Patel + SRE (cc'd)
- Structured output schema & validation: Laura Bennett + Priya (Acme)
- Production rollout: Laura Bennett + Acme ops

Next steps:
- I'll attach ACME_MAP_Draft_v2.xlsx with these owners and updated dates.
- Dev / Rishi, please confirm feasibility of the target bench dates and add any platform blockers to the Jira ticket INF-4123 before Tue sync.

Attachments: ACME_MAP_Draft_v2.xlsx

Best,
Marissa

Marissa / team —

Confirmed on the owners. Quick engineering notes and blockers I added to INF-4123:
- SDK: Python/Node SDKs are ready for examples; need 3rd-party CI keys from Acme to run e2e tests (request sent to Alex).
- Streaming: we'll enable prefix KV caching but need expected sequence length distribution from Acme before we tune the kernel selection.
- Tool-calling: webhook signing token flow is implemented; mutual TLS will require time for cert exchange and a testing window (est +2 weeks if they require mTLS).

I'll add short PRs to the SDK repo with example rehydration snippets and a small sample app we can run in your staging account. ETA for sample app: 2026-04-02.
